display_name: Durably roll back local the solet to the prior release
description: Plugin-namespace registration backing the service-interface verb service_interface::local_self_deployment_service::rollback_release. Operator-triggered DURABLE code rollback — DISTINCT from swap_rollback (the in-drain-window router re-point). Brings the prior MATERIALIZED release's code tree back up as a fresh process (spawned from that release's own venv/bin/python3 + re-pointed code/) and atomically flips the durable current/previous release symlinks, so it works at ANY time — post-drain, post-reboot — because both code trees persist on disk. Mechanism (design 2026-06-27 §4.5 PATH A): CAS the caller's expected_current_release against the live ReleaseManager.current_release FIRST (mismatch → FAILED stale_current_release with the actual current echoed, no spawn); read the ledger's previous release (None → FAILED no_rollback_target); spawn it as the opposite color; wait for register + TCP health probe; router.activate(prev_color); ReleaseManager.rollback() swaps current<->previous AFTER activate, F2-gated compensation on failure; quiesce the broken current (gating its own action-queue poller off before complete_swap is enqueued); enqueue the durable complete_swap finisher for the reactivated release's poller. The reactivated release is born is_active_color=True (C2 sidestepped — no cross-process flip). A second rollback_release rolls forward again (rollback toggles current<->previous) — undo/redo.
embedding_description: Roll the solet back to its previous release on macOS: rehydrate the prior materialized release, bring it up as the opposite blue-green color, and swap the durable current and previous pointers so the machine runs the older code again. Works at any time, including after the drain window closed or the machine rebooted. Takes a reason and a compare-and-swap guard against the live release.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: RestartResult envelope: status, restart_action_id, message, reason, expected_etag, dry_run, and the machine-readable reason_code partition field.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Lead with status. If 'queued', surface restart_action_id + the reactivated release. If 'failed', surface message + reason_code (system unchanged, retryable). If 'needs_intervention', surface message + reason_code prominently — a human must act before the next automated attempt is safe.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Operator-triggered durable code rollback of local blue-green solet to the prior materialized release.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: router_unavailable: ~/.ananta/runtime/<name>.router.sock not present or unreachable. status='failed'+reason_code is a coherent retryable refusal (stale_current_release: the live current moved under the caller — the CAS, checked first; no_rollback_target; activate_refused), NOT a crash. status='needs_intervention' is recovery-exhausted: rollback_target_unbootable (the previous release dir is gone/corrupt or never registered within the timeout) or compensation_incomplete (a failed swap's compensation could not complete; the durable current/previous pair MAY be incoherent).
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: If router_unavailable, install via plugins/macos_self_deployment_plugin/src/macos_self_deployment_plugin/blue_green_router/install_router.py and retry. On 'failed', address the named cause and retry. On 'needs_intervention', do NOT retry blindly — inspect ~/.ananta/releases/<name>/ (current/previous symlinks + state.json). Dead-solet cold-boot path is out-of-band: ReleaseManager.rollback() + re-launch via ananta.cli.
